## Load Packages and Data
Use the Rsubread package to map a yeast read file from the FGCZ.
```{r}
BiocManager::install("Rsubread", update=FALSE)
BiocManager::install("BSgenome.Scerevisiae.UCSC.sacCer3", update=FALSE)

# download the read data file
download.file("http://fgcz-gstore.uzh.ch/public/Yeast_Reads/20170313.A-G1_R1-sub.fastq.gz", "G1_R1-sub.fastq.gz")

# to view documentation for Rsubread enter:
browseVignettes("Rsubread")
```

```{r}
library(BSgenome)
library(BSgenome.Scerevisiae.UCSC.sacCer3)
library(Rsubread)
library(dplyr)
library(GenomicAlignments)
library(RVenn)
```

## Build Index and Align
Use *export* from the *BSgenome* package to write the genome as a fasta file on the local disk. Use *buildindex* and *align* from the *Rsubread* package to map the reads. Build the index s.t. at most 2GB of RAM is used. Run the alignment with 4 threads. 

Align to the genome with the RSubread::align function that does not explicitely look for spliced alignments. Do the alignment for the full length reads. Then run the alignment also a second time with fixed trimming of 10 bases from both ends, i.e. use align(….., nTrim5 = 10, nTrim3 = 10).
```{r}
export(BSgenome.Scerevisiae.UCSC.sacCer3, con="sacCer3-genome.fasta")
buildindex("sacCer3-Rsub", "sacCer3-genome.fasta", memory=2000 ) # generated index files are saved to the current working directory

align.stat <- align(
    index = "sacCer3-Rsub",            # basename of the genome index
    readfile1 = "C:/Users/zoe/OneDrive - ETH Zurich/Documents/ETHZ/24HS_MSc/STA426/week5/20170313.A-G1_R1-sub.fastq.gz",
    output_file = "G1_R1_alignment.BAM",  
    nthreads = 4
)

trim_align.stat <- align(
    index = "sacCer3-Rsub",            # basename of the genome index
    readfile1 = "C:/Users/zoe/OneDrive - ETH Zurich/Documents/ETHZ/24HS_MSc/STA426/week5/20170313.A-G1_R1-sub.fastq.gz",
    output_file = "trim_G1_R1_alignment.BAM",  
    nthreads = 4,
    nTrim5 = 10,
    nTrim3 = 10
)
```

## Question 1
For both runs (with and without trimming), what fraction of the reads aligns uniquely and multiple times?

WITHOUT trimming 72% of reads align uniquely, and 18% align multiple times (10% do not map).
WITH trimming the fractions are 74%, and 19%, respectively (7% do not map).
```{r}
# without trimming
1929371/2667280 # fraction of uniquely mapped reads (unique / total)
478892/2667280 # multiply mapped reads (multi / total)

# with trimming
1972065/2667280 # uniquely mapped reads
511032/2667280 # mulitply mapped reads
```

## Question 2
Are there reads that align the same in both cases?
Check the agreement of the alignments. Load the uniquely aligning reads. Use the function readGAlignments. Use the parameter settings to read also the read id, and the number of hits (NH).

Yes, there are 2'384'086 reads that align in both cases.
```{r}
sbp <- ScanBamParam(what = c("qname"), tag="NH") 
alignFull <- readGAlignments(file = "C:/Users/zoe/OneDrive - ETH Zurich/Documents/ETHZ/24HS_MSc/STA426/week5/G1_R1_alignment.BAM", use.names = TRUE, param=sbp)
alignTrimmed <- readGAlignments(file = "C:/Users/zoe/OneDrive - ETH Zurich/Documents/ETHZ/24HS_MSc/STA426/week5/trim_G1_R1_alignment.BAM", use.names = TRUE, param=sbp)

## aligning to the same location?
common = intersect(mcols(alignFull)$qname, mcols(alignTrimmed)$qname)

alignFull <- alignFull[match(common, mcols(alignFull)$qname)]
alignTrimmed <- alignTrimmed[match(common, mcols(alignTrimmed)$qname)]

ovlStatus <- poverlaps(granges(alignTrimmed), granges(alignFull), type="within") %>% as.vector() # check whether genomic range of trimmed are contained in full (granges extracts the alignment coordinates)
mean(ovlStatus) # proportion of true values
```

## Question 3
For those reads that align full and trimmed, do they align to the same location?

Roughly 95% of reads that align both full and trimmed align to the same location.
